clips.title: When to Use Claude Agent SDK? Agent Harness Explained
clips.why: A clear first picture of what an agent harness is and where the Agent SDK sits next to frameworks and the Claude Code CLI.
look: How he separates an agent framework, which gives you parts, from a harness, which is a working agent you configure.
How the Agent SDK compares with the Claude Code CLI you use in a terminal.
What the SDK already gives you, such as its built-in tools, so you do not write them yourself.
clips.after: Nova is our harness around this harness: query() runs Claude Code, and our code only decides the options and reads the result.

clips.title: Build & deploy agents with the Claude Agent SDK
clips.why: In under two minutes: the SDK as Claude Code in library form, and the loop of prompt, tools, observe, repeat.
look: The idea in the first chapter's title, Claude Code "in library form": the same agent as in your terminal, started from code.
The loop of prompt, tools, observe, repeat: each pass through it is what we call a turn.
clips.after: Every pass through that loop appears in your for await loop as assistant and user messages, and the loop ends with one result message.

practice.q: The compiler says: Property 'result' does not exist on type 'SDKResultMessage'. What is the right fix?

options.why: The cast hides a real case: error results have no final text, so you would print undefined and never notice the failure.
The success result is the only one with a result field. Narrowing first matches what the session really sends.

options.text: Read msg.message.content on the result instead
options.why: message.content belongs to assistant and user messages. The result message has no message field.

practice.q: Finish the loop header that reads a session's messages one by one.
practice.why: for await waits for each message as the session produces it, and the loop ends when the session ends.

practice.q: A session reads one file and then answers. Put its messages in the order they arrive.
items: system message with subtype init: model, version and tools
assistant message with a tool_use block asking for Read
user message with the tool_result: the file's text
assistant message with a text block: the answer
result message with subtype, is_error, cost and session_id
practice.why: init always comes first and the result always comes last. In between, each tool call is an assistant message followed by a user message with the tool's result.

practice.q: Complete the condition that marks a run green only when it really worked.
practice.hint: The field that is true when the turn ended on an API error.
practice.why: An API error can end the turn with subtype success. is_error is what tells the two apart.

practice.q: Your code imports query from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk" and tool from "@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk/core". What is wrong?

options.text: Nothing, both entries export the same functions
options.why: They export the same names, but they are separate bundles. Mixing them loads two copies of the SDK's classes and state.
/core exports tool() and createSdkMcpServer() as well as query().

options.text: One process should import from only one of the two entries
options.why: Pick the root for normal apps or /core for bundled ones, and use it everywhere in that process.
